study type: quasi-experimental design with a qualitative component
exposure: skin-to-skin contact during elective caesarean birth
cohort: Women undergoing elective caesarean birth and their newborns in a public hospital in metropolitan New South Wales.
finding: Skin-to-skin contact during elective caesarean birth significantly reduced the time to first feed and first breastfeed, increased breastfeeding on discharge, and was associated with improved maternal bonding and reduced anxiety and depression.
mod_finding: For women undergoing elective caesarean birth, skin-to-skin contact immediately post-birth was shown to improve early feeding outcomes, increase breastfeeding on discharge, enhance maternal bonding, and decrease maternal anxiety and depression.
